description: Found by the PQ-72 delegator (PR #109, merged 0deed94); client ruled a ticket on 2026-10-31. Today a quotes_checked attestation lasts as long as the span's text does, and it ignores the surrounding sentence and the program. So an edit can change the context so a previously checked span becomes a real claim about what a program prints, while the span stays checked. Mitigation today: any edit clears the affirmation and the review screen labels the span for whoever re-affirms. Not a contradiction of AC-73 as written: a mismatch still blocks unless that exact span was attested. Pinned behaviour: test_ac73_a_checked_quote_lasts_exactly_as_long_as_its_text in pipeline/tests/test_review.py, and the comment in pipeline/src/popquiz/review.py; both need changing if behaviour does. Decide first: what should invalidate an attestation (sentence changed, program changed, or any edit), keeping House rule AC-7 (never write down what a program prints). Acceptance: the chosen trigger unchecks the span, shown failing under its mutation; just test green; if AC-73's wording needs amending, that goes to the client.
title: An edit can turn a checked quote into a claim about output without unchecking it
